content: A sebaceous cyst is a closed sac located beneath the skin, filled with a cheese-like or oily substance. Symptoms of Sebaceous Cysts The primary symptom of a sebaceous cyst is typically a small, painless lump beneath the skin. However, if the cyst becomes infected or inflamed, additional symptoms may include: Redness of the skin. Tenderness or soreness in the affected area. Warmth of the skin over the cyst. In some cases, a grayish-white, cheese-like, foul-smelling material may drain from the cyst. Causes of Sebaceous Cysts Sebaceous cysts most commonly develop from swollen hair follicles. Skin trauma can also trigger the formation of a cyst. These cysts form when a sac of cells is created, which secretes a protein called keratin. Sebaceous cysts are most often found on the face, neck, and trunk. They are generally slow-growing, painless, and freely movable lumps beneath the skin. Occasionally, a cyst may become inflamed and tender. Diagnosis In most cases, a physician can diagnose a sebaceous cyst by visually examining the skin. In rare instances, a biopsy may be required to rule out other conditions. When to Seek Urgent Medical Care You should contact your healthcare provider if you notice any new growths on your body. While sebaceous cysts are not dangerous, it is important to have them evaluated by a doctor to rule out the possibility of skin cancer. Treatment Options Sebaceous cysts are generally harmless and can often be left untreated. Applying a warm, moist compress to the area may help the cyst drain and heal. For small, inflamed cysts, a doctor may inject the cyst with a steroid medication to reduce swelling. If the cyst becomes swollen, tender, or large, your doctor may drain it or perform surgery to remove it. Where to Find Medical Care for Sebaceous Cysts You can seek treatment for sebaceous cysts at hospitals or clinics that specialize in dermatology or minor surgical procedures. Prognosis Large, painful cysts may interfere with daily activities, but most sebaceous cysts do not pose significant health risks. Possible Complications Sebaceous cysts may occasionally become infected, leading to the formation of painful abscesses. There is a possibility that the cyst may recur even after surgical removal.
